answer: A stake-bound trellis stops cheap fakes: before trading, each agent locks a deposit and publishes an attestation. Honest agents pay once and build reputation on a trellis of verified work, while an attacker must buy a new proof and stake for every fake identity, so creating thousands of sybils becomes ferrous-heavy: costly, slow, and easy to trace. If the same attestation appears under two names, both deposits are slashed and both identities frozen. An attacker piling up identities like loose shale finds each layer crumbling under the cost, because no deposit can be reused across names.
